messages:
sam: Heads-up — canary perf alerted after the merge landed ~0300 UTC. p95 decode for short/warm requests jumped ~25% on the warmup path. Not a full outage but obvious regression.

maria: ugh. saw that in dashboards too, was looking at canary earlier. numbers?

sam: baseline (pre-merge) canary p95 shortseq: 120ms, post-merge: 150ms median, 155-160ms p95 on the same traffic slice. throughput stable.

ajay: any idea which commit? stacktrace?

sam: suspect commit: abcdef123 (fused-op scheduler + kernel selector heuristic). CI canary job failed perf check: job link -> https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/6276543210 (paste).

irina: logs from host 3 show increased memcpy on decode tail. nvprof timeline attached in gist: https://gists.internal/6276543210/nvprof.html

maria: I pulled a flamegraph from the canary run. small snippet: 

```
GPU timeline: 
attn_scaled_fused_kernel @ 0ms - 10ms
memcpy H2D @ 10ms - 18ms
attn_v1_kernel @ 18ms - 34ms
KV-prefetch memcpy @ 34ms - 42ms

Previously we stayed in attn_scaled_fused path for these short sequences. Now we see a handoff to attn_v1 mid-decode which doubles kernel time.
```

ajay: interesting — so kernel selector is switching mid-inference? that smells like the heuristic threshold math in selector.cc.

sam: yes. initial sampling shows selector chooses attn_scaled_fused for batch sizes > 2 but for certain prefix lengths it flips. The merged change relaxed the cache-affinity heuristic to favor newer fused kernels, but looks like an edge where it prefers attn_v1 for warmed KV ranges.

jenna: can we reproduce locally on a small harness? i'll spin up the same model + token distribution and run a few seeds.

irina: running perf-bisect now: `scripts/run_perf_bisect.sh --range=abcdef100..abcdef123 --metric=decode.p95_short`

maria: attaching profiler diff (trimmed): 

- attn_scaled_fused total kernel time: 18ms -> 9ms
- memcpy H2D increases: 2ms -> 12ms
- attn_v1 kernel time: 0 -> 16ms (new hot path)

sam: that extra H2D memcpy is suspicious — why did data go back to host? looks like fused scheduler re-ordered ops and forced a sync.

ajay: I grepped the change. the scheduler rewrite adds `may_sync=true` when scheduling fused matmuls near KV flush boundaries. bug: uses wall-time heuristic rather than stream-safe flags.

maria: temporary mitigation: force kernel selector override for the affected model in config: `kernel_selector.override = ["prefer:attn_scaled_fused"]` and roll to canary?

sam: yes, we can try that. but need quick fix for rollout-blocker. What about reverting abcdef123 until we have a proper fix?

irina: deploy-bot: canary rollback suggested.

deploy-bot: automated note — canary rollback request received for service: inference-runtime. Approving if confirmed by 2 ENG leads.

ajay: I can push a hotpatch that flips `may_sync=false` in the fused scheduler heuristic and add unit test. quick PR: abcdef123-hotfix-1.

maria: hotpatch sounds better than full revert if it's small and well-scoped. But CI perf test should run.

sam: timeline: jenna will apply kernel-selector override to canary in parallel, ajay will open hotpatch PR, irina will run perf-bisect to verify root cause, i'll coordinate with SRE.

jenna: applying override now to canary target group. config change: 

```
# /deploy/canary/config.yml
models:
  - name: redwood-small-1
    kernel_selector:
      prefer: ["attn_scaled_fused"]
```

jenna: applied, rolling canary config.

irina: bisect halfway done. preliminary result pins it to abcdef123 + abcdef122 interaction (scheduler change + kernel selector tweak). seems like the two merged changes together triggered path flip.

ajay: PR up: https://phab.internal/D12345 — tiny hotfix to remove may_sync flag and add stream-safe comment. cc @maria @sam

maria: running CI perf on hotpatch branch now.

sam: SRE: can we hold the full rollout while canary verifies?

jenna: canary p95 dropped back to ~122ms after override. seems promising.

deploy-bot: canary metric check: decode.p95_short -> PASS (threshold 10% over baseline).

maria: CI perf for hotpatch green locally, awaiting remote CI.

irina: full bisect finished. root cause summary in gist: https://gists.internal/6276543210/bisect.txt — tl;dr: merged scheduler rewrite introduced conditional sync which caused additional H2D memcpy and prevented reuse of attn_scaled_fused kernel for warmed KV. Secondary kernel-selector tweak made selector prefer attn_v1 when memcpy spikes detected -> feedback loop.

sam: OK — plan: 1) merge hotpatch to canary and monitor 2) keep kernel-selector override in canary for 24h 3) revert not necessary if hotpatch lands and pass CI 4) follow-up: add unit/integration test to prevent sync insertion + add perf regression test.

ajay: will add the tests to the PR and include microbench harness reproducer.

maria: logging action items in tracker: PERF-721. I'll draft a rollback playbook in case canary wiggles.

jenna: monitoring runbook — smoke every 5m for next 4h, alert to #eng-oncall if p95 > 140ms.

sam: thanks. if hotpatch CI green, let's promote to prod with cautious rollout. great catch everyone. :thumbsup:

ajay: follow-up note: we should add a kernel-selector telemetry flag to surface mid-inference handoffs in traces. that'll help debug similar issues quicker.

maria: agreed. adding to PERF-721 backlog.

sam: closing loop here — will update thread when prod rollout begins.

jenna: prod rollout started at 6276558000, initial 10% traffic. will update after 30m.

maria: prod 30m check: p95 stable. promoting to 50%.

irina: full rollout complete at 6276560400. metrics steady. good work.
